You wrote an entire article about my “junk history” responding to a 30 second clip that some other account posted while making no attempt to engage with the fleshed out points I made in the hour long documentary I just published on the subject (part 1 of 2). Yes someone is posting junk here, and I think it’s the guy fishing for a few cheap clicks on his blog by cherry picking 30 seconds to rebut rather than dealing honestly with my full point which I presented in great detail with citations.


S

My favorite part is the idea of some right wing racist extremist militant who is a big fan of both Trump and DeSantis. That’s a category that includes zero actual humans on Earth. These people don’t have a theory of mind for conservatives at all so they have no idea how to effectively slander us.

Literally nobody believes these hoaxes anymore but they keep trying anyway. You almost have to respect the commitment to the bit.


Ben Crump (@AttorneyCrump)

A historic Black cemetery in Palmetto, Florida, was vandalized, with graves damaged and “Trump” and “DeSantis” spray-painted across tombstones. Our ancestors deserve dignity in life and in death. Desecrating sacred burial grounds is hateful, painful, and unacceptable. We must protect Black history and honor the families impacted by this c

Did a deep dive on the data centers today on the show. Tried to assess the issue fairly and lay out the concerns in a reasonable way: 

piped.video/watch?v=wEm1Zp…

Another point about our cultural decline. We started watching the show Widow’s Bay. It’s really good. Fantastic writing. Perfect blend of comedy and horror. Last night’s episode was legitimately one of the finest episodes of television I’ve seen in years. 

If this same exact show came out in 2002, we’d probably remember it as an all time classic. But in 2026 most people haven’t even heard of it. It’s a blip on the radar. Another piece of content in the endless sea. You see it, or you don’t, and

But now the culture is programmed by a handful of Big Tech companies through algorithms. The old model had its issues but it was a shared experience at least, and driven by humans rather than machines. Also you’re leaving out the localized part of this. Every town had its radio stations, its video rental places. That seems obviously better for the soul than a fully atomized culture programmed algorithmically by trillion dollar tech companies and consumed mostly through little screens and an endl

I’m not against the technology itself. I think the technology is amazing, mind blowing. There are all kinds of totally valid and useful applications. All I’m saying is that we are not wrestling at all with the implications, and there are no limitations of any kind being placed on these companies as they race towards their goal of fundamentally transforming human society overnight. Reckless in the extreme.

Big Tech companies are sprinting forward, building data centers as fast as they can, sometimes using eminent domain to seize the land by force, making their AI more and more powerful, expanding the technology at lightening speed with no guardrails of any kind at all. Yet none of these tech gurus or any of their apologists have even attempted to explain what exactly all of the millions of people who lose their jobs, and the increasing numbers who lose their homes, all sacrificed on the AI altar,

Every decade in modern American history can be identified and defined by its own style, its own approach to music, film, fashion, its own aesthetic. That seems to have stopped right around 2010. The 2010s don't really have their own unique feel, even in retrospect. The 2020s certainly don't. We're more than halfway through the decade. What are the movies, music, style, and trends that this decade will be remembered for? It's like we fell into some kind of cultural blackhole 15 years ago.

It’s funny when right wingers applaud these kinds of comments from leftists. Liberals blame “white liberals” for not being woke enough, essentially. Blaming “white liberals” is just a way of saying that minority liberals are perfect and blameless in all ways.


The Post Millennial (@TPostMillennial)

Director Adam McKay says that "no group is worse than white liberals."

Video
  





— https://nitter.net/TPostMillennial/status/2054929933713956995#m

There's a reason that the 00s feel like the last real decade. Something happened in 2009. iPhones invented two years before. Then in 2009, Facebook rolled out its personalized algorithm-driven feed. Twitter and Instagram followed a few years later. I really think, if you have to point to just one culprit (though there are several), it would be this. The algorithm killed the monoculture more than anything else. We live now in a culture almost entirely shaped by the algorithm, which is to say that

Some people would say the culture froze earlier, like at the turn of the millennium. But I don't think that's true. The 2000s definitely had their own feel. If I referred to an "early 2000s comedy" or "early 2000s music," you'd know what I mean. The shift happened later, at the end of the 2000s, into the 2010s.

Thank you. My team does an incredible job on the history show. We’re proud of it.


P B (@PB06386212)

Your brilliant history show has reminded people that outside the mind-numbing conservative echo chamber, there’s still a genuinely fascinating, complex world out there worth exploring, questioning, and challenging.



— https://nitter.net/PB06386212/status/2054699675131797676#m

Of course I expected the “you’re talking about yourself!” comments. To some extent, yeah. I felt myself getting too repetitive on my show so we switched the format pretty drastically and started doing much more in depth analysis of a single topic per show. We’ve covered a very wide range of topics over the past few months, and for the most part the audience has responded positively to it.
